170ab2e15c28.q: Direct versus assisted acquisition — define both, and the paperwork each requires.
170ab2e15c28.h: Who places the order decides the lane and the documents.
170ab2e15c28.d: Direct: the requesting agency places the order itself against the servicing agency's contract — no written interagency agreement required, but the best-approach analysis is documented. Assisted: the servicing agency awards and administers on your behalf — a written interagency agreement signed by both parties, defining roles and unique terms, before funds move. And for any order against a non-DoD agency's contract over the SAT, a best-procurement-approach D&F: alternatives analyzed, schedule and performance weighed, the servicing agency's authority verified.

170ab2e15c28.q: When does the Economy Act apply, and what rides with it?
170ab2e15c28.h: It's the fallback authority — with a MIPR and a finding.
170ab2e15c28.d: 31 U.S.C. 1535 applies only when no more specific authority — schedules, GWACs — covers the buy. It rides on a MIPR plus a D&F finding the interagency acquisition is in the Government's best interest and the supplies or services can't be obtained as conveniently or cheaply from a private source, with at least one qualifying circumstance (their existing contract, their expertise, or specific statutory authorization). Citing the Economy Act for a schedule order tells the board you memorized a name, not a framework.

170ab2e15c28.q: Does money change color or clock when it travels to another agency?
170ab2e15c28.h: T-P-A rides in the MIPR envelope.
170ab2e15c28.d: No. Time, Purpose, and Amount travel with the funds — expiring O&M doesn't gain life at another agency, the bona fide need is still judged by the requesting agency's need in the appropriation's period, and the purpose statute follows the dollars. Parking expiring funds with a servicing agency to 'save' them is a Time violation with postage. Unobligated balances come home as what they are.

a901361401a3.q: LoC versus LoF versus LOGO — which clause on which contract, and what trigger?
a901361401a3.h: Fully funded, incremental, and the fixed-price cousin.
a901361401a3.d: Limitation of Cost — fully funded cost-type contracts: notice when costs will reach 75% of the estimate within the coming 60 days. Limitation of Funds — incrementally funded cost-type: the same 75% trigger applied to the allotted amount. LOGO — incrementally funded fixed-price CLINs: notice within 90 days of hitting 85% of the CLIN amount. In every case the notice is the contractor's duty, the contractor isn't obligated to perform past funding, and a ten-day warning at the ceiling means no automatic entitlement.

a901361401a3.q: Recite the financing order of preference.
a901361401a3.d: RFO Part 32: private financing; then customary contract financing — where performance-based payments are preferred (events, not costs; recoverable in default) and progress payments run at the clause and current class-deviation rates; then loan guarantees (rare); then unusual financing, requiring higher approval; and advance payments last — least preferred, most heavily approved, commercial advances capped at 15% of price.

a901361401a3.q: Which year's money pays whatever adjustment comes out of this?
a901361401a3.h: The appropriation that bore the need — and its expired window.
a901361401a3.d: The adjustment charges the appropriation that funded the original need — likely the prior year's O&M, now expired. Expired funds remain available for five years for exactly this: adjustments to obligations properly made when they were current — claims, terminations, equitable adjustments. After cancellation they're gone for every purpose. Reaching for this year's money because it's handy is a Time violation dressed as convenience.

4833bd501bdf.q: Recite the rights levels for technical data.
4833bd501bdf.h: Three levels, funding-driven, one converts on a clock.
4833bd501bdf.d: R-DFARS 227: unlimited rights — development entirely at Government expense; use, modify, release to anyone for any purpose. Government Purpose Rights — mixed funding; any Government purpose including competitive reprocurement under nondisclosure protections, no commercial use, converting to unlimited after the period (five years standard). Limited rights — entirely private expense; internal Government use and emergency repair or overhaul only.

4833bd501bdf.h: One level swaps names, and SBIR runs long.
4833bd501bdf.d: Unlimited and Government Purpose Rights mirror the technical-data levels. The private-expense level becomes restricted rights — use on one computer at a time, tight copying limits. And SBIR data rights protect for twenty years under current policy, transitioning afterward. Remember the definitional split: technical data is recorded scientific/technical information; computer software is programs and code — and you can't reverse-engineer software you hold under restriction.

4833bd501bdf.q: Walk the marking-challenge sequence — and the discipline while it runs.
4833bd501bdf.h: Written, sixty days, decision, appeal — and hands off meanwhile.
4833bd501bdf.d: Written challenge stating the grounds; the contractor has 60 days to justify the assertion with records — the burden of proof is theirs; unresolved, the CO issues a final decision; the contractor may appeal — 90 days to the agency board, 12 months to the Court of Federal Claims (RFO 33.205-6). Challenges run within six years after final payment or six years after delivery of the data or software, whichever is later, with no time limit where the data are publicly available without restriction, were provided without restriction, or the restriction was fraudulently asserted (R-DFARS 227.7103-13(d)(1)). The discipline: honor the markings until every appeal resolves — using challenged data as if unrestricted converts your challenge into their claim.

d4c7bcd10160.q: What are the four elements of the scope assessment?
d4c7bcd10160.h: Anticipation, type, period, and the cumulative ledger.
d4c7bcd10160.d: RFO Part 43: scope of the competition — would the original offerors have reasonably anticipated this change at award; contract type — FFP carries tighter scope than cost-type; period of performance — a reasonableness standard; and contract cost or price — the cumulative impact of ALL modifications, never just the one in front of you. Mod 14 is judged against the original award with mods 1 through 13 on the scale.

d4c7bcd10160.q: Define the modification types for me.
d4c7bcd10160.h: Two signatures' worth, plus the two accidents and the boundary.
d4c7bcd10160.d: Unilateral — signed only by the CO: administrative changes, in-scope change orders, option exercises, termination notices; the contractor keeps its REA right. Bilateral (supplemental agreement) — both parties; preferred for anything substantive. Directed change — a formal change order under the Changes clause. Constructive change — Government conduct alters the work without formal direction; equitable adjustment, asserted within 30 days of incurring costs. Cardinal change — beyond the original competition entirely: potential breach, and the Changes clause cannot authorize it.

d4c7bcd10160.q: What does the Changes clause actually cover — and what does it NOT?
d4c7bcd10160.h: Three things per contract family — and two famous exclusions.
d4c7bcd10160.d: Supply contracts: drawings, designs, or specifications; method of shipment or packaging; place of delivery. Service contracts: description of services; time of performance; place of performance. T&M adds GFP. What it does NOT cover: period-of-performance changes — those go by mutual agreement — and Government property changes, which ride the GFP clause. Reaching for the Changes clause outside its list is how in-scope theories quietly die.

2b7ae5c2864c.q: Recite the four-part GFP justification test.
2b7ae5c2864c.h: Interest, ledger, risk, and no alternative — all four.
2b7ae5c2864c.d: RFO Part 45: (1) furnishing the property is in the Government's best interest; (2) the overall benefit significantly outweighs the increased administrative cost; (3) it does not substantially increase the Government's risk; and (4) the requirement cannot otherwise be met. All four must hold, documented by the requiring activity — the PM — in an MFR to the PCO. The exception needing no justification: property furnished for repair, modification, or overhaul, where the property IS the requirement.

2b7ae5c2864c.q: What clauses ride with Government property?
2b7ae5c2864c.h: The foundational clause brings a six-pack with it.
2b7ae5c2864c.d: RFO 52.245-1, Government Property — the foundational clause — plus Use and Charges, and the R-DFARS set that always travels with it: IUID registry reporting, tagging/labeling/marking, loss reporting, property-management-system administration, and reporting/reutilization/disposal. All required whenever the property clause is in. That clause architecture is exactly what last year's informal loan skipped — which is why the damage had no owner.

2b7ae5c2864c.q: The range gets damaged mid-contract — who determines liability, and on what standard?
2b7ae5c2864c.h: A process, an administrator, and a risk allocation.
2b7ae5c2864c.d: The loss/damage machinery under the property clause: the contractor reports and investigates, the property administrator manages the process, and the CO determines liability under the contract's risk allocation — on a cost-type effort the contractor typically bears loss only where managerial personnel were at fault or the property system failed. Condition baselined at delivery is what makes any of that adjudicable — undocumented condition is how disputes become coin flips.

92cf433e8e97.q: Recite the UCA obligation caps and the definitization clock.
92cf433e8e97.h: Two percentages, one deadline, one extension.
92cf433e8e97.d: R-DFARS 217.74: obligations capped at 50% of the not-to-exceed price before the qualifying proposal, up to 75% after it. Definitization within 180 days of the qualifying proposal — or when obligations hit the caps, whichever comes first — extendable 90 days if the HCA finds it in the Government's interest. Obligate only consistent with the contractor's spend plan; no spend plan, no payment.

92cf433e8e97.q: When is a UCA justified in the first place?
92cf433e8e97.h: Three conditions — and two disqualifiers everyone tries anyway.
92cf433e8e97.d: Only when there's no time for negotiations, a binding agreement is needed so work can begin immediately, and waiting would cause genuine harm. Lack of planning and administrative convenience are never valid. Approval sits with the HCA, delegable (no lower than COCO under $50M), and the circumstances driving a UCA usually drive a Part 6 exception in parallel — urgency or one-source — so the J&A rides alongside.

92cf433e8e97.q: Why does fee come down at definitization?
92cf433e8e97.h: Weighted guidelines price risk — and months of actuals retired some.
92cf433e8e97.d: The weighted-guidelines fee prices the cost risk the contractor carries. By definitization, months of performance have converted unknowns into actuals — the risk the fee would have compensated has partly evaporated, so the fee follows the risk actually remaining. Pricing the performed portion on estimates when facts exist would pay a risk premium for risk already retired. Say it exactly that way; it's a favorite probe.

182bb3002d18.q: Business versus contract clearance — what does each approve, and where do UCAs fit?
182bb3002d18.h: Strategy gate, deal gate, and one deliberate exception.
182bb3002d18.d: Business clearance approves releasing a competitive solicitation or opening sole-source negotiations — the strategy gate. Contract clearance approves the negotiated result — the award, the deal gate. In competitive selections it attaches to the SSA's decision points. UCAs are the deliberate exception: no clearance at award — there's no price to bless yet — clearance comes at definitization.

182bb3002d18.h: Six rungs from the PCO to the Secretariat.
182bb3002d18.d: Under $10M: the PCO. $10M to $75M: three levels below the SCO. $75M to $200M: two below. $200M to $500M: one below — the OSF. $500M to $1B: the SCO. Over $1B: SAF/AQC. This $40M action clears three levels below the SCO — and no calendar, quarter-close, or handshake moves the gate.

182bb3002d18.q: What must the PNM tell the clearance reviewer?
182bb3002d18.h: The whole story — especially where the number moved.
182bb3002d18.d: The purpose of the negotiation, the acquisition and the parties, contractor systems status, any certified-data exception, what data the CO relied on, the Government's objectives versus the negotiated result — with every significant movement explained on facts — the profit or fee basis, and the statement that the price is fair and reasonable. A PNM that explains a $2.1M move in two sentences isn't a record; it's a request to take your word for it.

1793b05f993b.q: Recite the post-award stay rule precisely — and how it's overridden.
1793b05f993b.h: Two windows, take the later; override is written and high.
1793b05f993b.d: At GAO, a post-award protest triggers the automatic stay if filed within 10 days of award or 5 days of the required debriefing — whichever is later. Override requires written HCA authorization on one of two bases: urgent and compelling circumstances, or the best interests of the United States — and for a post-award override, within 30 days. Pre-award protests stay the award itself upon GAO's notice.

1793b05f993b.q: Compare the three protest venues for me.
1793b05f993b.d: Agency-level: fastest and least formal, roughly a 35-day target, self-correcting — and the protester can still go elsewhere after. GAO: the 100-day statutory clock, the CICA automatic stay, recommendations that are legally advisory but followed in practice — non-compliance is reported to Congress. COFC: full judicial proceedings, binding and appealable decisions, no automatic stay — the protester must win a preliminary injunction.

1793b05f993b.q: What are your responsibilities while the GAO protest runs?
1793b05f993b.h: Notify, assemble, state the facts, then implement.
1793b05f993b.d: Notify everyone concerned including the SSA; coordinate with Legal immediately; assemble the agency report; prepare the CO's Statement of Facts; support the Memorandum of Law; and if GAO sustains, implement the recommendations within 60 days — including paying protest costs where warranted. And if counsel finds a real defect mid-protest, voluntary corrective action beats riding to a sustain: faster, cheaper, and you control the remedy.

f1d79eb178f7.q: REA versus claim — give me the four differences.
f1d79eb178f7.d: Interest: accrues on a claim from receipt; none on an REA. Decision deadlines: the CDA puts the CO on a clock for claims; REAs have none. Preparation costs: allowable as contract administration for an REA; unallowable for a claim. Formality: claims are written, demand a sum certain, carry appeal rights, and require certification over $100K — plus DoD's separate REA certification above the SAT. Substance controls the label.

f1d79eb178f7.h: Six years back, sixty days to answer, two appeal doors.
f1d79eb178f7.d: Submission within 6 years of accrual. Certification over $100K. For claims over $100K the CO issues a decision within 60 days or states when it will issue; silence becomes a deemed denial and starts the appeal clock. Appeals: the Board of Contract Appeals within 90 days, or the Court of Federal Claims within 12 months. Over $500K, coordinate ADR potential — and every decision goes by certified mail with appeal rights stated.

f1d79eb178f7.q: Which pieces of a mixed claim like this one actually settle, and how do you close it?
f1d79eb178f7.h: Element by element, then one document that ends it.
f1d79eb178f7.d: Evaluate entitlement element by element — the lockout has clear Government causation; the extra reports need the constructive-change analysis; prep and counsel fees are unallowable in the claim lane and come out. Then negotiate a global settlement where the facts support one, and paper it as a bilateral modification with a release of claims — the release is what makes the settlement final. Whatever won't settle gets a written final decision, certified mail, appeal rights stated.

e9a973de709d.q: Walk the T4D runway, in order.
e9a973de709d.h: Cure, show cause, excusability, final decision.
e9a973de709d.d: RFO Part 49: cure notice — Government's intent, the failures, 10 days to cure (not required for pure late delivery; when in doubt, send it); show cause — demand the contractor explain why the contract shouldn't be terminated; excusability analysis — documented before the decision, not after; then the T4D notice as the CO's final decision, hard copy, with the required contents: the failures, liability for excess reprocurement costs, non-excusability, reserved rights, appeal rights.

e9a973de709d.h: Beyond control, without fault — three families.
e9a973de709d.d: Acts of God; acts of the Government in its sovereign capacity; and fires, epidemics, strikes, unusually severe weather — events beyond the contractor's control and without its fault or negligence. A subcontractor's failure excuses the prime only if the cause was beyond the control and without the fault of BOTH prime and sub, and substitute performance wasn't reasonably available. The fire here is why the excusability record gets built before any notice goes out.

e9a973de709d.q: And if your default is later found wrongful?
e9a973de709d.d: The T4D converts to a termination for convenience: instead of collecting excess reprocurement costs, the Government pays a settlement — costs incurred on the terminated work, reasonable profit on work performed, and settlement expenses. That conversion risk is the entire reason for the runway: every skipped step is a step the board of contract appeals will walk back through, with the Government paying for the shortcut.

781fc79ab088.q: What makes BAA evaluation lawful competition?
781fc79ab088.h: Announcement, criteria, independent review — against a standard.
781fc79ab088.d: RFO Part 35: broad public announcement; stated evaluation criteria; and independent scientific or engineering merit review — with each proposal evaluated against the published standard, not compared head-to-head. The market competed by proposing. The Government can fund all, part, or none, and award a contract or an assistance instrument. What a BAA cannot do is buy production units to a spec — that's an RFP wearing a lab coat.

781fc79ab088.q: Walk the SBIR phases — and Phase III's special properties.
781fc79ab088.h: Feasibility, prototype, production — and the third has no cap.
781fc79ab088.d: Phase I, feasibility — small, short, typically FFP. Phase II, prototype — larger, longer. Phase III, production — funded outside the SBIR set-aside, no dollar cap, no J&A required when it derives from competitively awarded Phase I/II work (the statutory 'authorized by statute' lane), and SBIR data rights persist. Document the derivation chain — and note: SBIR authorization has lapsed and been in flux recently, so verify the current program status before building a strategy on new starts.

781fc79ab088.q: When would you steer AWAY from an OT?
781fc79ab088.h: The trade only pays when it buys something.
781fc79ab088.d: Traditional performers, well-understood requirements, or flexibilities nobody actually needs. A 10 U.S.C. 4022 OT trades the mature protections framework — competition rules, cost principles, disputes machinery — for agility and nontraditional participation. Spend that trade only when it buys something real: a commercial tech company that won't take a FAR contract, prototype-speed terms a real schedule demands. 'Skipping the rules' is the dishonest reason, and boards can smell it.

eeb37836c1b8.q: What does the differing-site-conditions clause require before recovery — and why?
eeb37836c1b8.d: Written notice before the condition is disturbed, so the Government can investigate the site as found — that's the clause's bargain. A Type I condition differs materially from what the contract documents indicated; keep digging for a week and the evidence is gone, which is why the notice failure discounts recovery even when the entitlement is real. Honest merits, reduced by the investigation the Government lost.

eeb37836c1b8.q: What's the legal test for personal services?
eeb37836c1b8.d: Whether Government personnel exercise relatively continuous supervision and control over contractor employees — the employer-employee pattern: assigning daily tasks, directing how work is done, approving leave. That relationship is unlawful without specific statutory authority (RFO Part 37). Proximity and embedded seating don't create it; supervision does. The fix is always structural: direction flows through the PWS and the contractor's own management.

eeb37836c1b8.q: What bonds and protections ride a construction contract at this value?
eeb37836c1b8.h: Two bonds over $150K, and damages that must be forecasts.
eeb37836c1b8.d: Over $150K: a performance bond at 100% of the contract price protecting the Government's work, and a payment bond — no smaller — protecting subs and suppliers who can't lien Government property, plus a bid guarantee at solicitation. Liquidated damages, where used, must be a documented forecast of probable actual delay costs — punitive rates collapse as penalties. And the solicitation discloses the magnitude range, never the estimate.

370f23a93603.d: RFO Part 17: price still fair and reasonable on a fresh look; funds available; the option serves an existing need and is the best method; synopsized or exempt; contractor not excluded in SAM; performance considered — which is where the missed reports and the near-miss live; and written notice by the contract's date. The PM's verbal promise satisfies none of them and binds nothing.

370f23a93603.q: The 'extra monitoring' — ratification lane or constructive change? Sort it for me.
370f23a93603.d: Sort by what happened: work OUTSIDE the contract's scope that someone without authority commissioned is an unauthorized commitment — the RFO 1.405 ratification lane, six elements, COCO or HCA approval by dollars. Government conduct that CHANGED existing in-scope work is a constructive change — equitable adjustment through the Changes clause via an REA. Environmental monitoring the contract never contained points toward ratification; either way, the practice stops in writing today.

370f23a93603.q: Can you even exercise the option with an open UAC investigation on the same contract?
370f23a93603.h: The gates don't pause — but one of them absorbs it.
370f23a93603.d: Yes, if the gates honestly pass — there's no rule suspending options during a ratification investigation. But the performance-considered gate absorbs the whole picture: the surveillance failures, the safety near-miss, and a contractor performing unpriced work on a range officer's say-so. Document the option decision on that complete record. If the record says extend, extend with corrective expectations in writing; if it says compete, a year is exactly enough time to start now.

3141b8cd4cf5.q: Severable versus non-severable — define both and fund both.
3141b8cd4cf5.h: Benefit as performed, or one product at the end.
3141b8cd4cf5.d: Severable services deliver benefit as they're performed — custodial, maintenance, help desk: fundable with annual money for a period up to 12 months, which may cross fiscal years. Non-severable services produce a single end product — one study, one overhaul: a bona fide need of the award year, fully funded up front, and they may run past a year. Fund a non-severable effort incrementally and you've violated Time and Amount at once.

3141b8cd4cf5.q: What duration limits cap the structure you just proposed?
3141b8cd4cf5.h: The services rail and the emergency spare.
3141b8cd4cf5.d: Base plus all options can't exceed five years on SCLS-covered service contracts (RFO 22.1002-2(a)(2), under 41 U.S.C. 6707(d)) — so base-plus-four is exactly the ceiling. The extension-of-services clause holds six more months in reserve for a transition emergency, and DoD ordering periods run past ten years only on a written head-of-agency exceptional-circumstances determination (R-DFARS 217.201-270), and that is a Head of Agency determination. The five-year rail is why 'one award forever' was never on the table.

3141b8cd4cf5.q: Could you obligate year-two money at award using the availability-of-funds mechanism?
3141b8cd4cf5.h: That clause times an exercise; it doesn't advance an appropriation.
3141b8cd4cf5.d: No. Availability-of-funds language lets the Government exercise an option on time subject to funds, with the obligation attaching when the appropriation arrives — it preserves the unilateral right across the fiscal seam. What it cannot do is obligate money Congress hasn't appropriated or stretch this year's O&M across next year's severable period. Each option year gets funded by its own year's money, exercised through its own gates.

9ebdcf249c43.q: Does one offer defeat 'adequate price competition'?
9ebdcf249c43.h: The exception is about expectation and the price you can prove.
9ebdcf249c43.d: Not automatically — the competition was full and open, and one responsive offer received under competitive expectations can still support the exception. But with one offer, the pricing burden rises: support fair-and-reasonable with the IGCE, prior-buy history, catalog and market comparisons, and document why the price stands on its own evidence. If the support isn't there, request data other than certified and analyze — the count of offers never substitutes for price analysis.

9ebdcf249c43.q: What would you actually ask the no-bids — and why does it matter?
9ebdcf249c43.h: The answers either fix your solicitation or clear your file.
9ebdcf249c43.d: Why they passed: requirement shaped wrong, period too short, bundling too big, terms too risky, incumbency assumed unbeatable? Informal, documented conversations. The answers matter twice — they either reveal a solicitation defect worth fixing before award, or they confirm the competition was genuinely open and the field chose not to play, which is exactly the record that defends a single-offer award and improves the next cycle.

9ebdcf249c43.q: Where would certified cost or pricing data enter this picture?
9ebdcf249c43.h: Check the threshold and the exceptions before asking.
9ebdcf249c43.d: At $1.7M this action sits below the certified-data trigger, so certification never enters — and even above it, you'd run the RFO 15.403-2 CLAWM exceptions first, where adequate price competition may still apply to a competitively solicited single offer. What you can always demand is data other than certified sufficient to price the action. Know the ladder: threshold, then exceptions, then the data ask sized to what the file actually needs.

5ecfeace5e45.q: When is a cure notice NOT required?
5ecfeace5e45.h: Three cases — and a default instinct when unsure.
5ecfeace5e45.d: Pure failure to deliver on time — the delivery schedule was the cure period; defaults based on a contract clause that doesn't require notice; and construction under its own default clause. When facts are mixed — like performance failures alongside lateness — send it: a needless cure notice costs ten days, a missing one can cost the termination on conversion. Here the complication isn't the notice; it's the waiver.

5ecfeace5e45.q: How exactly does the COR's 'keep at it' email change your posture?
5ecfeace5e45.h: Encouragement after a missed date can waive the schedule.
5ecfeace5e45.d: Post-delinquency encouragement to continue performing — from someone the contractor reasonably heard as the Government — can waive the delivery schedule, making the original date unenforceable. The cure: re-establish a firm, reasonable delivery date in writing, show-cause framing, restoring an enforceable schedule before any default posture. And the channel lesson rides along: CORs don't direct, and every 'keep going' from now on comes from the CO in writing.

5ecfeace5e45.q: Walk the excusability test on the subcontractor's plant fire.
5ecfeace5e45.h: Beyond control and without fault — counted twice.
5ecfeace5e45.d: A sub's failure excuses the prime only when the cause was beyond the control and without the fault or negligence of BOTH the prime and the subcontractor, AND the supplies weren't obtainable from another source in time. So: was the fire genuinely beyond the sub's control? Did the prime manage the risk — second sources, inventory, diligence? Could substitute generators have been had? Build that record before choosing between default, waiver-repair, or riding out the delay.

e131654f29c2.q: What are the exceptions to fair opportunity under RFO 16.507-6?
e131654f29c2.h: Six — and two of them are braided into this scenario.
e131654f29c2.d: (1) Unacceptable delay in meeting an urgent need; (2) only one awardee capable — unique or highly specialized circumstances; (3) logical follow-on to a fairly competed order; (4) satisfying the minimum guarantee; (5) authorized or required by statute; (6) for DoD, NASA, and the Coast Guard, the order satisfies one of the RFO 6.103 exceptions to full and open competition (10 U.S.C. 3406(c)(5)), with the public-interest one unavailable unless Congress is notified. Small business set-asides are not an exception at all — RFO 16.507-6(c) makes them a separate authority, carved out of the justification, approval and posting requirements. This scenario braids the first two — the 60-day operational order and the original firmware authorship — and the justification gets written on whichever the evidence actually carries.

e131654f29c2.q: Approval and posting for your $1.4M justification?
e131654f29c2.h: Same ladder as a J&A — find the rung.
e131654f29c2.d: The Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity — the name RFO 16.507-6(d)(2)(i) requires — rides the J&A tiers: the ordering activity CO's own certification serves as approval at or below $900K, Competition Advocate above $900K to $20M, HPA/PEO to $90M ($150M DoD), SPE above. At $1.4M: the Competition Advocate. Post the redacted justification to SAM.gov within 14 days of the order — 30 under urgency. A same-week justification at this tier is entirely achievable, which is the honest answer to 'skip the paperwork.'

e131654f29c2.q: Why does 16.507 govern here instead of a CICA urgency exception?
e131654f29c2.h: Orders under existing vehicles are a CICA carve-out.
e131654f29c2.d: Task and delivery orders under existing IDIQs are one of the lanes where CICA doesn't attach — the SAMO carve-outs: SAP, statutory authorities, in-scope mods, and orders under existing vehicles. Competition discipline for orders lives in RFO 16.507 fair opportunity instead — same values, different machinery. Citing 6.103-2 urgency for a task order tells the board you know a name; explaining why 16.507 governs tells them you know the architecture.

e2a8b964dfec.q: Walk your response steps, in order.
e2a8b964dfec.h: Legal, facts, containment, affidavits, MFR, determination.
e2a8b964dfec.d: Notify Legal immediately. Gather the facts and documents — who was in the room, what exactly was said. Contain: the support contractors' firms confirm no further dissemination, with signed affidavits and NDAs. Get an MFR from the analyst who disclosed. Notify affected parties as Legal advises. Then the written determination: does this disclosure impact the procurement? No impact — the record goes forward for concurrence and the selection proceeds. Impact — the HCA decides: proceed, investigate, cancel, or disqualify.

e2a8b964dfec.q: Is a past-performance rating really source selection information?
e2a8b964dfec.h: It's an evaluation result in an active selection.
e2a8b964dfec.d: Yes. Evaluation results — including past-performance ratings — in an active source selection are squarely protected: information that could give an offeror a competitive edge. That's why every source-selection document carries the SSI cover sheet, why distribution runs through the PCO as conduit, and why 'it was just one sentence at a staff meeting' doesn't change the analysis. The venue made it a disclosure; the email four days later made it evidence of impact.

e2a8b964dfec.q: What obligations attach to the incumbent now that they may hold protected information?
e2a8b964dfec.h: Mirror image of the Government's containment.
e2a8b964dfec.d: Stop, safeguard, report, and don't use. An offeror that receives protected information must not act on it — and the capture lead's email seeking to 'address performance concerns before FPRs' looks like acting on it, which compounds the violation. Their conduct after receipt becomes evidence in the impact determination: an offeror that reports promptly may survive with mitigation; one that exploits the leak volunteers itself for the disqualification analysis.

6a46384cf480.q: Which colors of money, and what clocks run on each?
6a46384cf480.d: O&M — one year for new obligations. RDT&E — two years. Procurement — three. MILCON — five. After the window, funds expire: no new work, but available five more years for adjustments to properly made obligations — claims, terminations, equitable adjustments. Then cancelled: gone for every purpose. Her $6M of current RDT&E has two years of obligational life — the plan's problem is the out-years, not the start.

6a46384cf480.q: Can integration and test ride O&M in years four and five?
6a46384cf480.h: Purpose follows the work, not the calendar.
6a46384cf480.d: No. Integration and test of a developmental system is development — RDT&E work under the Purpose Statute, 31 U.S.C. 1301: funds only for the purposes Congress appropriated. Calling late-stage development 'kind of operations' is a misappropriation exposure, and knowing obligation of the wrong color invites the Anti-Deficiency analysis behind it. That branch of her plan dies in the strategy meeting, on the record — kindly, but dead.

6a46384cf480.q: So how do you lawfully structure a $40M effort with $6M in hand?
6a46384cf480.h: Incremental funding with the right clause — and honest ceilings.
6a46384cf480.d: A cost-type development contract, incrementally funded under Limitation of Funds discipline: the ceiling stated honestly, funding allotted as appropriations arrive, the contractor's 75% notice machinery running, and no obligation ever ahead of or above the money — that's the ADA guardrail. Or phase the effort into separately funded awards matched to real appropriations. She can start immediately with $6M of honest scope; what she can't do is promise $40M the Treasury hasn't produced.

95e08834394b.q: Type I versus Type II differing site conditions?
95e08834394b.h: Differs from the documents, or differs from the ordinary.
95e08834394b.d: Type I: subsurface or latent physical conditions differing materially from what the contract documents indicated — asbestos the specs never mentioned, exactly this case. Type II: unknown physical conditions of an unusual nature, differing materially from what's ordinarily encountered in work of this character, even if the documents were silent. Type I turns on the documents; Type II on the ordinary. Both require the written notice before disturbance — which this contractor nailed.

95e08834394b.q: What does a DSC actually entitle the contractor to — and what not?
95e08834394b.d: An equitable adjustment — the cost and time consequences of the changed condition: abatement, resequencing, schedule relief — negotiated on the documented record. It is not a termination right: the contractor continues performing as directed while the adjustment is worked. 'Pay me for work done and release me' is a convenience-termination outcome, and that decision belongs to the Government, not to the discovery.

95e08834394b.q: The customer's 'just shrink the scope' idea — what is it really, and how would you do it honestly?
95e08834394b.h: Deleting work the Government still wants finished elsewhere has a name.
95e08834394b.d: Descoping the contaminated rooms to 'call it complete' is a partial termination for convenience wearing a modification costume — the Government is ending part of the work for its own reasons. Done honestly: a partial T4C with a proper settlement — costs incurred on the terminated portion, reasonable profit on work performed, settlement expenses — or a deductive change honestly negotiated if the work is genuinely no longer needed. The label matters because the settlement machinery and the record follow it.
